items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I got the trumpet player's name. Frankie Newton. ... Great big guy. Well, he took Coleman Johnson's place when Cole went to Europe with this band. ... He could play, man. And he was such a nice guy.

ctx.x: Well, high, you know -- whoo-oo-o! (imitates trombone) He'd slide, you know, up to it. (Inaudible) and dropped down to low notes, to low with the range, you know? He had that. And nobody else played like that. And he went to New York, and he kind of upset everybody playing like that. In fact, he did a good job because he's still playing in New York, and he's played a lot of the name bands, and I got a letter from Dickie Wells -- it's been quite a few years now; he wrote me and wanted to know if I had my brother's…
You know? But you have to come to New York, one of these kind of things, and I was tied up then, couldn't do it. But it was -- I got the trumpet player's name. Frankie Newton.
